objective: Prove that in every network of equally spaced rule-60 rings with law (12,12) contacts every row after the first has even total parity, so no later row is open; show that reading binding from the insertion row as if it were open gives the stage's persistence for every schedule, and compute that read natively (a contact binds a ring from row t0 at lag T unless its value can be computed from the other cells of row t0 on the states the history allows) every contact fails at some lag, with growth and without it.
status: Proved 2026-11-09 (by hand; finite claims checked exactly; the native reading computed): every cell of a rule-60 network with law (12,12) contacts is read by exactly two cells, so every row after the first has even parity and is not open; read as if the insertion row were open every contact persists, but read natively from any later row of a tube that never grows every contact fails to bind each of its rings at some lag (rows 1 to 7, four tubes). The breakage under growth while running is not a reading artefact.
title: No row after the first is open, so knots cannot be read from the last growth event
